A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OVSegDT and retain identifiable architecture, training, and HM3D-OVON experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original navigation results, training-strategy comparisons, component ablations, training curves, and observation-removal experiments in its main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 reports revised navigation experiments and additional entropy-sensitivity, lighting-robustness, hardware-performance, and real-robot results.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a semantic reward combining geodesic progress and changes in ground-truth target-mask area. It replaces v2's adaptation using size-filtered ground-truth masks with PPO fine-tuning on YOLOE predictions, jointly using semantic reward and auxiliary segmentation supervision. The architecture and EALM gate remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The retained HM3D-OVON coverage is extended with controlled lighting perturbations in Appendix H and physical iRobot Create 3 demonstrations involving visible and initially hidden targets in Appendix J. v2 contains simulation evaluations without these additional environmental conditions or physical-robot scenarios.

E2.justification: The benchmark baselines and switching-strategy comparators in Tables 1 and 2 retain the same membership, including Uni-NaVid, VLFM, TANGO, MTU3D, and EarlySwitcher. DagRL is reused in the new failure analysis; the additional entropy-related methods discussed in Appendix K are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes component evaluation from ground-truth to YOLOE masks. The observation ablation replaces the dummy 'table' text embedding with zeros, and the reported success reward changes from +1 to +2.5. New protocols include entropy-threshold sweeps, photometric perturbations, segmentation-error metrics, and training a 105-degree camera-FoV variant for robot demonstrations.

E4.justification: v3 adds entropy-threshold sensitivity analysis, a navigation-failure taxonomy, segmentation-error and lighting-robustness tests, and real-robot case studies. Table 3 also tests the separate and combined contributions of semantic reward and segmentation loss under predicted segmentation. Existing training curves and detector-confidence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed means and standard deviations and describe three-run, one-sided unpaired t-tests. Revised p-values and additional statistical result rows accompany changed experiments without establishing a different uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: For the revised final configuration, Table 1 changes val-unseen SR/SPL from 40.1%/20.9% to 44.7%/20.6%, while Table 4 changes collisions from 24.7 to 45.4. Component and observation-ablation outcomes also change, and failure, robustness, hardware, and robot results are added. These replacements involve different training and adaptation configurations.

T1.justification: v3 adds a mathematical semantic-reward definition, an action-space-dependent rationale for entropy thresholds, and formal augmentation and IoU-based segmentation-event definitions in Appendix H. These are limited formal additions; the existing PPO/EALM equations remain substantially unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: v3 redefines a main contribution around jointly using segmentation loss and semantic reward for predicted-mask adaptation, replacing the earlier emphasis on the auxiliary segmentation objective alone. It explicitly claims the first lightweight RGB-only demonstration of strong unseen-category generalization and reduces the headline collision-reduction claim from twofold to 10%.

C2.justification: v3 explains why low PPO collision counts can reflect early failure, interprets calibration and fine-tuning through recognition errors and improved viewpoints, and discusses the increased collisions accompanying predicted-mask adaptation. Appendix J adds a concrete near-goal safety limitation attributed to the reward balance. The earlier segmentation-dependence and free-form-instruction limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies a 15M-step fine-tuning budget, reward coefficient and clipping, lighting-augmentation parameters, and deployment hardware and camera details. v2 leaves its adaptation budget unspecified. Core hyperparameter tables and the code URL remain, but v2's CPU, Ubuntu version, and system-RAM disclosure are removed.

R1.justification: New Appendix K substantially expands EALM's positioning against entropy-guided augmentation, distillation, curriculum learning, test-time adaptation, SAC, and SafeDAgger. v3 also attributes the semantic reward to Staroverov et al. (2025) and adds PPO and generalized-advantage-estimation references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are substantially rewritten, with introductory arguments condensed and reordered. v3 introduces a numbered section hierarchy, an appendix guide, a lettered supplement, and acknowledgments, while removing the reproducibility checklist. These changes reorganize substantial retained material.

P2.justification: v3 adds entropy-sensitivity plots, robot photographs and trajectories, and failure, segmentation-error, augmentation, and hardware tables. Tables 3 and 4 gain reward and latency columns. Existing confidence-threshold plots are regrouped horizontally, and tables throughout are restyled and reduced in size.

improvement.justification: The predicted-mask component ablations in v3 Table 3 address v2's reliance on ground-truth masks to establish component benefits. New sensitivity, failure, lighting, and deployment studies substantially strengthen validation, while increased collisions and near-goal risks are explicitly discussed. Robot evidence remains qualitative, and reporting problems such as Table J's memory units limit particular claims, but the stronger evidence and clearer limitations provide a substantial overall improvement.
